rv.q: For the first time in forever, the show actually feels like “Now.”
The true difference, though, lies in the piece's shift from commercialized kitsch to camp sincerity.
They elevate “Cats,” and certainly make it work for a new moment where queens now sit on thrones unimaginable in 1981.
But now along comes a thrilling reconception at the Arts Center that not only rescues Cats from the oversize junkyard but lifts it, like Grizabella herself, to unexpected heights.
It’s impressive, it’s exhilarating, and perhaps most striking of all for a musical so long deemed so much fluff, it’s not just about cats.
The hottest club in New York City right now is downtown Manhattan's Arts Center, home to a must-see musical revival you never knew you needed

(No coincidence that a huge rainbow fan with the word “Pose” on it is for sale in the lobby.) Much care has been taken in the grafting of the queer onto the weird. There is an official ballroom consultant and also a gender consultant. Both the cast and the creative team feature participants in ballroom competitions.
Those adjectives are also a perfect fit for the ballroom setting and make for a really fun night at the theatre.

Admittedly, even at the end of this lengthy extravaganza, you may still not really understand what a “jellicle cat” is, but you will be jealous of your friends and neighbors if they get to see this groundbreaking production and you don’t.
Not only is this Cats different from any you have ever seen before, it is the most dynamic musical show to be seen in New York right now.
Imagine my surprise when Cats: The Jellicle Ball, the new adaptation of the material now at the Arts Center, turned out to be a plentiful source of dazzle, fun and joy.
There's no denying how much fun this production is – and how even a flawed show can find a path to rebirth
